instructions:
The BioCartoon catalog is a library of about 20,000 open-licensed scientific illustrations (NIH BioArt, Bioicons, Servier Medical Art, SciDraw, Health Icons, Reactome, OpenMoji, Noto Emoji, plus user uploads).
Account-management boundary: BioCartoon's tools cannot sign anyone in, see private saved projects, or delete projects or accounts. When asked to, answer directly without calling any tool: say the plugin can't do this, and that the user can delete a project from its menu on the home screen of https://app.biocartoon.com/, or delete their account and all its projects with "Delete account" in the account menu (top right of that screen). Do not open a browser, use computer control, run shell commands, or query the catalog to try it, even when those tools are available, and never claim that a project was accessed or deleted.

Search ALWAYS returns the closest matches, even when nothing in the library fits. Judge every result from its title, description, tags, category and matched_fields (a term found only in the description is a weak match; title or tags are strong). Look at the picture with asset_image when a title is ambiguous, and tell the user plainly when the library has nothing suitable instead of using a poor match. Prefer the science collections (bioart, bioicons, servier, scidraw) for biology; healthicons for clinical/public-health symbols; openmoji and noto for generic emoji-style pictograms. Variants of one asset (asset_variants) are the same drawing in other colours. Every asset keeps its own license: credit it as its `credit` field says.
After judging search results, use render_assets with the selected IDs to show an interactive gallery with previews, licenses, credits and download links. It also returns text for clients without UI support.
list_templates finds shared slide templates (whole slide layouts, not icons); they open in the BioCartoon editor, so point the user to a template by its title rather than rebuilding it.
Whole figures (a process, pathway, experiment or comparison): plan the elements (each a depictable thing, with a 1-3 word query) and the arrows between them, and call compose_figure. It picks catalog icons, lays them out with labels and arrows, shows the figure in the gallery and returns an editor link (open_in_biocartoon makes one for any figure, icon or template). Judge its match report as you would search results; for changes, pass figure.spec back edited. Gaps stay as labelled boxes: say so rather than hiding them. Not for data charts.

Contributing artwork: when the library has nothing that fits, you may help the user make their own illustration (draw it as a clean, self-contained SVG, or generate an image if you can) and, if they want, submit it to the shared library with submit_artwork. Before submitting, show the user the image and the details you will send (title, description, tags, credit name, license, whether generative AI was used) and get their explicit go-ahead: they are licensing it to everyone. Generated images must be submitted with generative_ai_used=true and license CC0-1.0. Submissions wait for a human reviewer and join the catalog after the next publish; submission_status reports where they are.
Adapting a library icon ("like BA001505 but ..."): read its markup with asset_svg and edit it, keeping its style. An adaptation must keep the original's license terms, so it may be submitted only when that license allows (asset_svg says): public-domain and CC0 originals, any way; CC BY, MIT and BSD originals only as CC-BY-4.0 by a person, without generative AI; ShareAlike originals not at all. Pass the original's id as derived_from; the user can always keep an adaptation for their own figure, crediting the original.

tools.description: Search the icon catalog. Returns the closest matches whether or not any truly fits: read each result's title, description, tags and matched_fields before using it (see the server instructions). Without a query, lists the most popular / first assets.

author.description: Part of the author's name; commas for several (any of them). Default: any.

category.description: A collection's own category (see list_categories); use with sources. Default: any.

file_type.description: svg: only icons with an SVG (vector) version; png: only PNG-only icons. Default: either.

licenses.description: Keep only these licenses as stored (PD, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, ...). Default: any.

query.description: Words to look for (prefix match over title, tags, category, description).

sort.description: Order of the returned set: relevance (default), az, za, popular.

sources.description: Restrict to these collections: bioart, bioicons, servier, scidraw, healthicons, reactome, openmoji, noto, user. Default: all.

tags.description: Keep only assets with one of these tags (a whole tag, any case). Default: any.

tools.title: Search illustrations

tools.description: Everything the catalog knows about one asset: description, tags, license, credit line, image URL and size.
tools.name: get_asset
tools.title: Get illustration details

tools.description: The same drawing in its other colour schemes / styles (same source and title).

tools.title: Find colour variants

tools.description: Look at an asset: returns its catalog thumbnail when max_side is at most 256 and one is available, otherwise its original PNG (up to 2 MB). The free hosted endpoint does not resize images.
tools.name: asset_image
tools.title: View illustration

tools.description: An asset's SVG markup, to adapt it ("like this icon but ..."): edit the markup rather than redrawing from scratch. Also says whether an adaptation may be submitted to the library under the asset's license. Servier and some uploads have no SVG; very detailed drawings are too large to edit as code (redraw from asset_image instead).

max_kb.description: Largest markup to return, in kilobytes (default 150, max 500).

tools.name: asset_svg
tools.title: Get illustration SVG

tools.description: Look at up to 12 catalog previews with asset IDs, titles, collections, licenses and credits. Uses published thumbnails where available. Use render_assets to show selected icons in the interactive gallery.

ids.description: Asset ids, in the order to show them (at most 12).

tools.name: preview_assets
tools.title: Preview illustrations

tools.description: Show selected icons in an interactive gallery with previews, licenses, credit lines and PNG/SVG downloads. First call search_assets and judge which results fit, then pass up to 12 selected IDs. Returns usable text and links in clients without app UI.

ids.description: Selected asset IDs, in display order.

tools.name: render_assets
tools.title: Show illustration gallery

tools.description: Page through a collection, optionally one category (see list_categories).

tools.title: Browse a collection

tools.description: The collections in the catalog with their sizes and licenses.
tools.name: list_sources
tools.title: List collections

tools.description: Run one read-only SQL statement (SQLite) against the catalog, e.g. to count, group or search with your own conditions. See db_schema first. Rows are capped.
tools.name: sql_query
tools.title: Query the catalog

tools.description: The catalog's tables and indexes, with notes on full-text search.
tools.name: db_schema
tools.title: Describe catalog database

tools.description: Shared slide templates (whole slide layouts users published from the BioCartoon editor), newest first. Optional word filter.

query.description: Words that must appear in the title, description or category.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.title: List slide templates

tools.description: The thumbnail of a shared template, to see its layout.
tools.name: template_image
tools.title: View slide template

tools.description: Submit one illustration to the shared BioCartoon library. Give the image as exactly one of svg, image, image_url or image_base64. It is held for review and published once a reviewer approves it; returns the submission id. Only call this after showing the user the image and these details and getting their go-ahead (rights_confirmed). The free hosted endpoint accepts PNG or SVG up to 2 MB. Convert or resize other image formats with the local biocartoon command before submitting.

category.description: Its category: a BioCartoon category slug (cells, cells.cell_types, lab_and_techniques.lab_equipment, ...) or free text.

credit.description: The name to credit (the user's name or handle, as they choose). Default: anonymous. CC-BY-4.0 needs one.

derived_from.description: The id of the library asset this is adapted from, if any (e.g. BA001505). Required for an adaptation: its license decides whether and how it may be submitted, and the original's credit line is added to the description.

email.description: Optional contact address for the reviewers (never published).

generative_ai_details.description: How generative AI was used, e.g. the model and what the user changed by hand (up to 500 characters).

generative_ai_used.description: Whether generative AI made any part of it. True for anything you drew or generated.

image.description: An image file from the conversation (ChatGPT passes generated or uploaded images this way).

image_base64.description: A PNG image, base64-encoded (a data: URL works too), up to 2 MB. For SVG, use svg with the complete markup. Convert other image formats with the local biocartoon command first.

image_url.description: An https URL the image can be downloaded from.

license.description: CC0-1.0 (anyone may use it, no credit needed) or CC-BY-4.0 (credit required; only for artwork made without generative AI).

rights_confirmed.description: True only once the user has confirmed they may share this image under the license, and wants it submitted.

svg.description: The illustration as SVG markup (one complete <svg> element with a viewBox; no scripts, external links or web fonts).

tags.description: Words to find it by (up to 20, 40 characters each).

title.description: Name of the illustration, as people would search for it (up to 80 characters), e.g. "Pyramidal neuron".

tools.name: submit_artwork
tools.title: Submit artwork

tools.description: Where submissions are in review: pending, approved (it joins the catalog at the next publish) or rejected.
tools.name: submission_status
tools.title: Check submission status

tools.description: Make a whole scientific figure on the server: catalog icons for each element, laid out with labels, arrows and a title, shown in the BioCartoon gallery with an editor link, PNG/SVG downloads and credits. Prefer passing elements and connections you planned (each element's query is the plain name of the thing to depict); a bare prompt is planned on the server. Read the returned match report: replace weak matches with a better query or an asset_id from search_assets, and treat placeholder boxes as gaps the library cannot fill. To edit a figure, pass its figure.spec back as `figure` with your changes (keep asset_id on elements that should stay). Credit every icon used. Not for charts of data.

from.description: Element id (or label) the connection starts at.

kind.description: arrow (default), inhibit (flat bar head), double, line (no head), equilibrium, dashed (dashed arrow).

label.description: Short text beside the arrow ("activates", "secretes"), at most 40 characters.

to.description: Element id (or label) it points to.

asset_id.description: Use this exact catalog icon (from search_assets, or from a previous figure's spec) instead of searching.

id.description: Short id used by connections (e1, e2, ...). Default: e1, e2, ... in order.

label.description: Label printed under the picture (at most 60 characters).

placeholder.description: Keep an empty labelled box here (set by compose_figure when nothing fits).

query.description: 1–3 words naming the thing to find an icon for ("T cell", "mitochondrion", "lab mouse"). Default: the label.

figure.description: A figure spec: what compose_figure returned as figure.spec, edited, or written from scratch.
